newsitem.title: PERU: Lima shrs end down on New York fall, weak economy.
newsitem.headline: Lima shrs end down on New York fall, weak economy.

text.p: Shares on the Lima stock exchange closed down Thursday in thin trade, as falling prices on the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) and a weak local economy caused some investors to sell stocks, brokers said.
Friday, volume would remain meager and New York was again likley to dictate the Lima market's direction, they added.

Thursday, the General Index .IGRA fell 1.41 percent to 1,400.2 points, while the blue-chip Selective Index .ISEL dropped 2.13 percent to 1,976.9 points, according to preliminary figures. In 1,302 trades, volume was 27.5 million soles ($10.7 million).

Some investors were also starting to worry about a possible conflict between Peru and Ecuador, whose simmmering border dispute has traditionally flared up around the December to February period, said Lorenzo Wong of brokerage Intercapital.
"In addition to the negative news on the economic front, we are seeing speculation over a possible conflict with Ecuador," he said.
Tension between the two neighbors, which fought a brief border war early last year, rose last month when Peru said it had bought a squadron of sophisticated MiG 29 jets.
Quito claimed the purchase was excessive and could lead to an arms race.
Thursday, benchmark Telefnica del Per led the market down as it fell 2.97 percent to 4.90 soles on volume of 1.81 million shares.

Luz del Sur, which saw the government fix a 3.10 per share price Wednesday in its sale of a 30 percent stake in the electricity distributor, closed down 1.59 percent to rest at the 3.10 sol mark on volume of 324,000 shares.
